subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the crab's proportions and orientation—facing +Z, sized like a small stylized rock crab around 24cm wide—and starting to plan the skeleton hierarchy with a root body joint.

Now I'm working through leg construction, deciding each leg needs a coxa-merus-carpus-propodus-dactyl chain, and the claws need articulated upper/lower pinchers. For the carapace, I'm leaning toward a flattened, non-uniformly scaled sphere with a mottled brick-red paint layered with orange and cream spots, and working out how the body's vertical placement and scale should align with where the legs attach near the floor.

Adjusting body height so the carapace sits raised with the underside slightly above ground, then adding scattered knob textures and small spiky teeth along the front rim using filtered surface points and spike geometry. I'm also placing the eye stalks as separate jointed parts offset from center.

Now I'm working out the mouth as a small upper and lower jaw pair, with the lower plate attached to a dedicated jaw joint, then moving on to the leg structure—setting hip positions along the body edge for each side and planning the hip-to-knee path outward and upward.

Plotting each leg's joint chain from hip through knee, carpus, and tip to mimic a real crab's leg bend, with front legs angled further forward and back legs angled back so the stance spreads naturally.

Setting leg radii to taper from thick to a pointed tip with rounded start caps, hexagonal cross-section, and reusing the shared body paint for coloring.

Now I'm figuring out the leg bands with darker tips blending into the leg paint, planning 8 legs with multiple joints each for a smooth skinned sweep. For the claws, I'm working out the chain positions for a raised big claw on the left side going out and up into a pointing gesture, versus a smaller lowered claw on the right.

Still writing arm chain geometry...

Still working out the pincher geometry...

Still shaping the pincer geometry...

Still tuning tooth and dactyl geometry...

Simplifying the radius taper to a fixed array instead of a formula, then moving on to defining the smaller right-side claw with its own scale and arm point positions for shoulder and elbow.

Shaping the palm with a swept radius profile between wrist and elbow, sizing it oversized relative to the arm but proportionate to the carapace, considering elliptical cross-sections for the width.

Now I'm thinking through paint for the claw -- red with orange speckles and darker fingertips, body-matched palm color -- and scattering a few small knob spheres onto the palm surface. I'm also working out the joint naming in the chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist) to figure out which joint position corresponds to the palm tip.

I'm fixing the chain to use four names (shoulder, elbow, carpus, wrist) with the tip derived from the chain, then attaching the palm bone and pincher joint to that tip, and setting up tapered arm sweep radii. For the barnacle detail, I'm figuring out how to place a small cone-like lathe shape on the shell surface using a downward ray hit, then defining its profile points so the lathe revolve closes properly into a rounded barnacle form.

Now I'm planning three seaweed strands draping off the back of the shell, using wavy catmull-rom paths with olive-green banded coloring, plotting rough offset points so they rise up and flop over naturally without clipping into the shell.

For the ribbon shape, I'm using a box-section sweep that tapers in width along its length, adding small olive bladder spheres at intervals for texture, and rigging the whole thing to the body bone so it moves with the creature using vector offsets from the hit frame.

Now I'm setting up the skeleton: a root body joint, hips and leg chains all parented off it. For the carapace, I'm layering a countershade effect over the speckled pattern so the back reads darker and the belly lightens toward cream, plus adding side bands and a front rim near the shell's leading edge.

Adding the shell flange and spike teeth...

Checking that the eye stalk positions sit correctly against the carapace surface, confirming the base is embedded at the right height and the eyeball tip clears the shell properly.

Now I'm working out the mouth placement: a small dark upper box with a jaw joint hinge, positioning everything slightly in front of the carapace rim and setting the color to a cream tone.

Setting up the paint palette next—red and dark red mottling with orange and cream speckles for the shell texture, then countershading toward a cream belly for softer contrast underneath.

Adding knob bumps with varied sizes and dark-tipped leg paint bands, plus pointed dactyl tip sweeps with hip-relative radius tapering...

Checking P1 clears the rim top properly. For the leg rig I'm naming the joint chain hip/knee/carpus/foot/toe per side, with claws using an arm-role chain. Now starting the claw function definition...

Writing palm sweep geometry...

Still tuning finger and palm proportions...

Adjusting pinch tips and finger geometry...

Finishing the dactyl base position with the opposite direction vector, then setting up the spike helper function for sweeps with flat starts, scattering stick-like knobs on the palm surface, and weighting the arm bone to the palm. I'm planning the remaining elements like seaweed and barnacles using surface sampling and downward raycasts for placement on the carapace.

Writing barnacle lathe profiles...

Adjusting the seaweed droop so it drapes more naturally over the shell's rear edge rather than floating in open air, then defining the strand's color gradient and tapering ribbon cross-section.

I'll keep a single plain color per strand for simplicity, add olive holdfast/bladder spheres at anchor points, and plan the final export structure with imports for the builder, rng, paint utilities, and catmull spline. Now I'm positioning lateral spikes along the shell's rim, placing their bases near the edge span.

Placing five front teeth around the front rim using angular steps, computing each tooth's base position on the rim ellipse and its direction and size. I've checked the ground contact points (leg tips at y=0, body bottom slightly raised) look fine, so I'm ready to write the final code.
